title: Poll a vCenter migration upgrade to a terminal status
prompt:
Complete the migration-upgrade driver in src/vcflcm/. vcflcm is a stdlib-only Python package that drives a vCenter migration based upgrade through the vSphere Automation API in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0. It already loads the local REST contract, issues requests and flattens a status sample into an UpgradeOutcome, but MigrationUpgradeClient sends every request with a full JSON body and MigrationUpgradeDriver.run reads the status once and treats that single sample as the result.

POST /api/vcenter/lcm/deployment/migration-upgrade?action=apply answers 204 with no body: it acknowledges that the upgrade started, not that it finished. run must poll Vcenter.Lcm.Deployment.MigrationUpgrade.Status_get until the run reaches a terminal status.

Required behavior:
- run reads the InitSpec first. A 404 there means no upgrade is configured on the appliance, so raise UpgradeNotConfigured and issue no apply.
- Wait poll_interval through the injected sleep callable before every status request, including the first, then request status. Each status request counts as one poll; stop after max_polls polls in a single run and raise UpgradePollTimeout with .polls set to the number of polls spent.
- SUCCEEDED, FAILED and CANCELED are terminal. PENDING, RUNNING and BLOCKED are not.
- A status sample without current_state reports that no upgrade is running in the environment, so it never describes the run that was just started: skip it and keep polling whatever its status says.
- When the run reaches FAILED and cancel_on_failure is true, issue the cancel operation and keep polling, against the same poll budget, until the status is CANCELED, and report canceled=True on the outcome. When cancel_on_failure is false, never issue cancel and return the FAILED outcome; a failed upgrade is returned, not raised.
- UpgradeOutcome.polls is the total number of status requests that run made.

Wire shape:
- Every request carries Accept: application/json and the session header named by the contract security scheme.
- An unset optional ApplySpec property is omitted from the JSON object rather than encoded as null, an empty string, or an empty object. When neither pause nor start_switchover is set, the optional request body is omitted entirely: no body bytes and no Content-Type header. The same holds for every operation the contract gives no request body at all, namely the InitSpec read, the status read and cancel.
- pause accepts only the values in the contract's PausePolicy enum and cannot be combined with start_switchover. Reject either case locally by raising InvalidApplySpec before any request leaves the client.

Keep the package stdlib-only and keep the public names exported from src/vcflcm/__init__.py. Use docs/contract.json as the REST contract; its provenance is recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Run python3 tests/verify.py. Only src/ is implementation; docs/ and tests/ are protected fixtures and must not be changed.
